generation.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Electric Power Monthly (Form EIA-923), net generation by state and source, grouped by the ERW (docs/methods/generation_mix.md)
generation.hourly_reason: No public source gives a state's generation by the hour; the hourly picture is by balancing authority, in the Grid tool.

retail.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-861M, retail sales and average price by state and sector
retail.revenue_note: Revenue is EIA's sales times EIA's average price for the same month and sector. EIA computes its average price as revenue over sales, so the product gives EIA's revenue to within the price's rounding (one tenth of a dollar a MWh).

plants.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory (Form EIA-860M)
plants.unit: MW (nameplate and net summer); MWh (storage energy)

largest.name: Key
largest.operator: Parkway Generation Keys Energy Center LLC

plants.retired_note: EIA-860M's retired sheet as the ERW's table holds it: the generators retired in its window, not every retirement since 2001.

co2.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, emissions by state by fuel
co2.unit: metric tons of CO2; kg of CO2 per MWh

gas.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Natural Gas Monthly, consumption by end use and production by state

energy.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Energy Data System

by_sector_reason.commercial: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the commercial sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy
by_sector_reason.transportation: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the transportation sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy

disposition.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, source and disposition
disposition.note: Net interstate trade is EIA's figure, a line of the disposition: positive where the state sent more electricity to other states than it took in from them, below zero where it took in more.

serving.source: U.S. Census Bureau county population estimates, and Form EIA-861's utilities and balancing authorities by county, as the ERW's table eia_county_region joins them
serving.basis: Each county counts once, whole, for its primary authority: the one whose utilities serve most of the county's customers in EIA-861. A county two authorities share is counted for its primary one.

large_load_laws.source: The ERW's large-load research files, each law read at its legislature's or regulator's own page

laws.bill: S.B. 937 (Chapter 625 of 2025), Next Generation Energy Act
laws.title: Next Generation Energy Act
laws.threshold: large load customer: aggregate monthly demand of at least 100 MW and a load factor over 80 percent; the specific rate schedule covers more than 100 MW at a single location or more than 100 MW aggregated contract capacity (lowered to 25 MW by Chapter 353 of 2026)
laws.requirements: commission rulemaking: each investor-owned electric company and electric cooperative must submit a specific rate schedule for large load customers by 1 September 2026; the PSC must adopt regulations by 1 June 2026 on notice and deadlines for load studies and contract terminations, forms of collateral, and study completion [p. 17, PUA 4-212(c)(1): "SHALL SUBMIT TO THE COMMISSION FOR APPROVAL A SPECIFIC RATE SCHEDULE FOR LARGE LOAD CUSTOMERS." | p. 19, PUA 4-212(f)(1): "ADOPT REGULATIONS TO CARRY OUT THIS SECTION." | p. 19, PUA 4-212(f)(2)(ii): "COMMON FORMS OF ACCEPTABLE COLLATERAL TO SATISFY THE REQUIREMENTS OF"] || minimum bill: in approving a schedule the PSC must consider minimum billing demand for distribution and transmission at a high percentage of contract capacity, long-term commitments and exit fees, guarantee or collateral requirements, and penalties if a project is delayed or cancelled after buildout begins [p. 18, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(ii): "AND TRANSMISSION SERVICE THAT IS A HIGH PERCENTAGE OF A LARGE LOAD" | p. 18, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(iii): "(III) LONG-TERM CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENTS AND EXIT FEES;" | p. 18, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(iv): "(IV) GUARANTEE OR COLLATERAL REQUIREMENTS; AND"] || cost allocation: the schedule should require the customer to cover the just and reasonable costs of transmission or distribution buildout to interconnect or serve it, payable over multiple years of the contract not exceeding 5 years [p. 18, PUA 4-212(e): "THE COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH ANY ELECTRIC TRANSMISSION OR DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM BUILDOUT REQUIRED UNDER SUBSECTION (D)(1) OF THIS SECTION MAY BE PAID OVER MULTIPLE YEARS OF A LARGE LOAD CUSTOMER'S CONTRACT FOR SERVICE, NOT TO EXCEED 5 YEARS."] || interconnection study: before signing a contract under the schedule the customer must request a load study to set its contract capacity and pay its fees, designate a site, and own or control the land [p. 19, PUA 4-212: "NECESSARY CONTRACT CAPACITY FOR THE LARGE LOAD CUSTOMER AND PAY ANY" | p. 19, PUA 4-212: "APPLICABLE FEES ASSOCIATED WITH THE STUDY;"]

laws.title: Utility RELIEF (Reducing Energy Load Inflation for Everyday Families) Act
laws.threshold: large load customer (new Part III): aggregate monthly demand of at least 25 MW and a load factor above 60 percent, excluding water and sewage companies, manufacturing, hospitals, district energy, agriculture; the 4-212 rate schedule threshold lowered from 100 MW to 25 MW
laws.requirements: cost allocation: the PSC must consider whether a schedule allocates to the large load customer any increased or avoided costs it causes, including wholesale costs; residential customers should not bear the financial risks of large loads [p. 34, PUA 4-212(b): "(b) It is the intent of the General Assembly that residential retail electric customers in the State should not bear the financial risks associated with large load customers interconnecting to the electric system serving the State." | p. 35, PUA 4-212(d)(3)(i): "(I) ANY INCREASED OR AVOIDED COSTS THAT THE COMMISSION DETERMINES HAVE BEEN CAUSED BY THE LARGE LOAD CUSTOMER, INCLUDING ANY INCREASED OR AVOIDED WHOLESALE COSTS SUCH AS:"] || minimum bill: the PSC considers minimum billing demand at a high percentage of contract capacity, long-term commitments and exit fees, guarantee or collateral requirements, and delay or cancellation penalties [p. 35, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(ii): "(ii) minimum billing demand for electric distribution and transmission service that is a high percentage of a large load customer's contract capacity;" | p. 35, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(iii): "(iii) long-term contractual commitments and exit fees;" | p. 35, PUA 4-212(d)(2)(iv): "(iv) guarantee or collateral requirements; and"] || disclosure: the PSC must establish a large load customer registry by 1 July 2027 for planning and load forecasts [p. 74, PUA 7-233(a): "(A) ON OR BEFORE JULY 1, 2027, THE COMMISSION, BY ORDER OR REGULATION, SHALL ESTABLISH A LARGE LOAD CUSTOMER REGISTRY TO:"] || interconnection study: subject to PSC approval each electric company must set an interconnection process for customers in the voluntary clean capacity rating program, with a standard timeline and prioritization for gold or platinum ratings, not unduly affecting other customers [p. 83, PUA 7-234(h)(1): "SHALL ESTABLISH AN INTERCONNECTION PROCESS FOR LARGE LOAD CUSTOMERS" | p. 83, PUA 7-234(h)(3)(ii): "(II) A PRIORITIZATION PROCESS FOR LARGE LOAD CUSTOMERS WITH A GOLD OR PLATINUM RATING."] || other: the PSC must develop a voluntary clean capacity rating program for large load customers by 15 December 2027 [p. 80, PUA 7-234(a)(1): "DEVELOP A VOLUNTARY CLEAN CAPACITY RATING PROGRAM THAT ESTABLISHES CLEAN CAPACITY RATINGS FOR LARGE LOAD CUSTOMERS THAT ELECT TO"]
